column1: # scripts/fleet-package-versions.tsv — observed package versions across the fleet.
# WHAT THIS IS FOR. PORTING-MATRIX.md's footnotes state where the fleet sits relative to
# a recorded floor. Those sentences enumerated a dozen distro versions in prose, and prose
# goes stale silently: footnote 34's jq line was corrected twice in one day — once for
# Alpine (#902) and once for Fedora (#904) — because nothing could disagree with it.
# This file is the data those sentences assert. gen-porting-matrix.sh renders it into the
# marked block in that footnote, and check-porting-matrix fails when the two diverge. The
# REASONING stays hand-written prose beside the block; only the enumeration is generated.
# WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. It cannot notice that a distro shipped a new version — nothing here
# reaches the network, deliberately, because this generator runs inside an offline audit.
# What it does is make staleness VISIBLE: every row carries the date it was checked, and a
# row past FRESH_DAYS is reported as due for re-verification. "Nobody has looked in 90
# days" is a fact you can act on; "as at time of writing" is not.
# FORMAT — tab-separated, first field is the record type:
#   floor <tool> <version>
#       The recorded floor. at-or-below is DERIVED by comparing each row against it, so a
#       row cannot claim a status its own version contradicts.
#   ver <tool> <target> <version> <verified> <source>
#       One observation. <verified> is ISO date. <source> names where it was read, because
#       "1.8.2" is worth nothing without it — Repology splits some projects across
#       version-named entries and reports false absences (dotfiles-Alpine#170), so a row
#       read there is weaker evidence than one read from the distro's own index.
# RE-VERIFYING. Check the row's source, update <version> and <verified>, run
# `make gen-porting-matrix`, commit both. Ordering here is display order.
